readout_other: Visually-evoked cortical potentials recorded via bipolar electrodes placed in cortical areas of both hemispheres, in response to repeated light flashes
direction_notes: Ultrasonic irradiation of the lateral geniculate nucleus reversibly suppressed the visually-evoked cortical potential: the primary response was reduced to less than one-third of its original amplitude and the secondary response to practically zero at the termination of irradiation, with complete recovery apparent 30 minutes after exposure.
safety_notes: The effect was produced by a dosage of ultrasound which does not cause any histologically observable lesion in the tissue.

exposures.label: Ultrasonic irradiation of lateral geniculate nucleus

timing.protocol_description: With a suitably chosen sound level and with an exposure time in the range from 20 to 120 seconds, it has been possible to produce reversible suppressions of various components of the elicited electrical response in the visual cortex. The focus of the sound beam is placed successively in and around the region of the lateral geniculate nucleus.
